sources.entry: JuiceMount - Mounts a NAS as a real Finder volume and streams video in blocks through a local SSD cache, with offline pinning.

summary.one_liner: JuiceMount is a beta, self-hosted macOS app that mounts a NAS (running JuiceFS over MinIO and Redis) as a real Finder volume, streaming only the video blocks you touch into a local SSD cache with offline pinning.
summary.what_it_does: JuiceMount mounts storage on a self-hosted server as a macOS Finder volume at a consistent path, so NLEs like Premiere, Resolve, and Final Cut see a local drive. Files are stored as 4 MB JuiceFS blocks, and only the blocks being read are fetched and cached on the local SSD. Folders can be pinned for offline use with a prefetcher and per-folder progress, and an offline mode fails un-pinned reads quickly instead of hanging Finder. An optional write spool acknowledges writes on local SSD and uploads them in the background with SHA-256 verification. A local SQLite metadata mirror and a Finder-tuned NFS server on 127.0.0.1 handle directory listings, and a menu-bar app shows health and upload status and includes a filename search window.
use_cases: edit video directly off a NAS on a Mac
share one media library across several editors
pin a project to work offline while travelling
replace per-seat cloud editing storage with self-hosted storage
browse and search a large NAS volume from Finder
let a teammate open a project without relinking media
how_to_run: Server: cd juicemount/server, edit docker-compose.yml for disk paths and MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD, then docker compose up -d
Download the notarized JuiceMount.app from Releases and drag it to /Applications, or build from source with ./scripts/build-app.sh and ./scripts/install.sh
On first launch, use the Setup Assistant to enter the Redis URL and optional S3 endpoint override, then click Start
Enter the admin password once at the mount prompt; /Volumes/<name> appears in Finder
notable: Only the 4 MB blocks touched are transferred, so scrubbing a large file pulls a small fraction of it over the network
Finder mounts via a loopback NFS server with a local SQLite metadata mirror, instead of raw FUSE, for faster directory opens
The on-disk format is the standard open JuiceFS format, so the stock juicefs client can read the volume without JuiceMount
Write spool acknowledges writes on local SSD and drains them to the NAS in the background, with crash recovery
Explicitly no telemetry, no update check and no File Provider extension
caveats: Beta and pre-1.0; macOS 14 or later only, tested on Apple Silicon, Intel untested
Requires self-hosting a server stack (Redis, MinIO, Docker or TrueNAS) and macFUSE plus the separately installed juicefs binary
Heavy simultaneous multi-editor use has not been soak-tested; cooperative locking is on the roadmap
Needs an admin password prompt once per session to mount; the write spool is off by default and un-spooled writes fail when the server is unreachable
